newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-MCFARLANE AND GOOSEN TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THE WEATHER.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MCFARLANE AND GOOSEN TAKE ADVANTAGE OF THE WEATHER.

text.p: Briton Ross McFarlane, yet to win in 14 years on the European Tour, fired a six-under-par 66 for a share of the early lead with South African Retief Goosen on the second day of the Benson and Hedges International on Friday.

The pair were tied on eight-under-par 136 with half the field having completed the second round. Glen Turner of New Zealand, who led with five under after the opening day, and Ireland's Christy O'Connor, who was second one stroke behind, had yet to start their round.

McFarlane's round would have been a course record but that was snatched from his grasp just a few minutes earlier when Eduardo Romero of Argentina shot a 65 to be two strokes off the pace on 138 and level with three other players, Britons Ian Woosnam and Lee Westwood and Patrik Sjoland of Sweden.
Woosnam had a four-under-par 68 and Westwood and Sjoland both shot 69.
McFarlane had nine birdies and three bogies in his round while Romero had seven but did not drop a shot.
"I played fantastic. It was my best round this year," the Argentine said.
McFarlane said: "My prime objective this year is to win a tournament. I've been near four or five times. Now I hope I've found the secret."
The leading players all took advantage of much more tranquil weather following the blustery cold that bedevilled the first round but stronger winds were forecast for the afternoon.

Sjoland, who will celebrate his 26th birthday on Tuesday and is in only his second year on the European Tour, enjoyed a spectacular patch when he reeled in five shots to par in the space of four holes.

Following his first round three-under-par 69, Sjoland had successive birdies at the fourth, fifth and sixth then eagled the 498-yard par-five seventh to go temporarily eight under but then had three bogeys before pulling back a shot on the final hole.
